The accuracy evaluation is reasonably broad, covering long-input, long-generation, and reasoning workloads across six model configurations and several relevant dropping and retrieval baselines. FreeKV generally remains close to full-KV accuracy at a 2,048-token budget.

The reported efficiency gains are substantial: up to 13.74× over ArkVale on the tested A100 PCIe system, with results across two models, two workload regimes, and several batch sizes. weaknesses: The central algorithmic premise is insufficiently validated. High cosine similarity between adjacent queries does not necessarily imply high overlap of selected top-k pages or small attention-output error. The paper provides no direct correlation analysis, selected-page overlap measurements, correction frequency, per-head failure analysis, or accuracy/latency curves over the correction threshold. Averaging similarity within a GQA group may also conceal a changing individual query head.

There is no accuracy ablation separating previous-step reuse, fine-grained correction, group-consistent pooling, and the page-summary design. Consequently, the evaluation shows that the complete configuration works at selected hyperparameters but does not establish which mechanisms are necessary or how robust they are.

The systems evaluation is narrow and under-specified: it uses one A100-40GB/PCIe platform and only 7–8B models, with no measurements on the evaluated 14B models, other interconnects or GPUs, larger contexts, throughput-oriented serving, peak GPU/CPU memory, or transfer volume. Timing methodology, warm-up, number of repetitions, and variability are not reported, and a full-KV reference is absent from the latency plots.

Baseline fairness is difficult to assess. Quest and RaaS are modified to use group-consistent pooling, ShadowKV is extended with periodic SVD updates despite not natively supporting long generation, RazorAttention uses a different effective cache budget, and Quest is omitted from end-to-end latency results. The paper does not validate that these adaptations preserve the original baselines' quality or use comparably optimized implementations.

The stochastic accuracy results lack confidence intervals or significance tests. Reasoning evaluation uses only 50 MATH500 and 50 GPQA problems, LongGenBench relies on a single LLM judge, and several reported differences are small or even exceed full-KV performance, making sampling and judging noise a plausible explanation. Task-specific choices of the sink/window sizes and correction threshold receive no tuning or sensitivity analysis.

The claimed O(B) GPU-memory complexity omits the page summaries stored on GPU, whose size grows as O(L/p), as well as caches and recall buffers. No measured memory results are provided despite memory scalability being a central motivation.

Reproducibility is weak: there is no code or artifact, and important implementation details such as the inference framework, kernels, cache replacement behavior, initialization, synchronization, and overlap scheduling are missing. The conceptual novelty is also moderate because temporal reuse, layout conversion, and double buffering are individually familiar ideas, while distinctions from closely related temporal attention-prediction or sharing methods are not experimentally established.

The central proxy assumption needs stronger validation: high cosine similarity between adjacent queries does not necessarily imply stable top-page selection. The paper does not measure page-set overlap, attention-output error, or correction false-negative rates, and thresholds are selected on the same task families used for evaluation rather than through held-out calibration.

The stated O(B) GPU-memory complexity is not literally correct because GPU-resident page summaries grow as O(L/p). Likewise, the broad claim of full latency hiding is overstated when correction places selection and recall back on the critical path and measured correction rates reach 0.52 on difficult tasks.

strengths: FreeKV addresses an important deployment bottleneck with a coherent algorithm-system design: speculative retrieval and selective correction are paired naturally with hybrid CPU/GPU layouts and streamed recall.

The accuracy evaluation is unusually broad, covering long-input, long-generation, and reasoning tasks across several Llama, Qwen, and DeepSeek-R1-derived models. At a 2,048-token budget, FreeKV generally remains close to full-KV accuracy.

The reported efficiency gains are substantial: FreeKV approaches the latency of dropping methods and improves over retrieval baselines across two models, multiple batch sizes, and varying input/output lengths.

The cumulative efficiency ablation identifies the contributions of hybrid layouts, double buffering, and speculative retrieval, while the appendix studies thresholds, group-consistent selection, query-similarity generalization, and correction rates.
The manuscript is clear, well organized, and technically intuitive, with useful diagrams explaining the pipeline and concurrency.
weaknesses: The headline comparison does not adequately control the systems substrate. Hybrid layout alone supplies up to a 10.5x speedup and appears applicable to competing retrieval methods, yet ArkVale and other baselines are not evaluated with the same optimized layout and transfer machinery. The incremental gain from adding speculative retrieval after the systems optimizations is only about 1.9x, making the claimed 13.7x method-level advantage difficult to interpret.

The claimed O(B) or fixed GPU-memory complexity is inaccurate as written: FreeKV explicitly keeps page summaries for the entire context on GPU, requiring O(L/p) storage, and selection also scans these summaries. No measured peak-memory results are provided, LongBench inputs are truncated to 64K, and scalability toward the motivating million-token setting is not established.

Efficiency evaluation is restricted to one A100 PCIe system and two 7–8B models. There are no larger-model results, alternative interconnects, multi-request serving throughput, tail latency, recall bandwidth, utilization measurements, or repeated-run/error-bar information. The claim of full latency hiding is therefore stronger than the presented evidence, especially when correction rates reach 0.43–0.52 on difficult tasks.

Accuracy comparisons have important uncertainty and fairness issues. Thresholds are selected using the same benchmarks on which results are reported; stochastic reasoning experiments use only 50 MATH500 and 50 GPQA problems without confidence intervals or paired-seed analysis; and LongGenBench relies on an LLM judge without validation details. Moreover, several baselines are modified to use one group-consistency rule, while FreeKV receives a separately optimized rule, which can materially affect accuracy.

High adjacent-query cosine similarity does not by itself imply stable top-k page selection or small attention-output error. The paper does not measure selected-page overlap, retained attention mass, trigger false negatives, or the correlation between cosine similarity and actual retrieval error, leaving the correction rule primarily empirically motivated.

Reproducibility is limited by missing implementation and timing details, including framework and baseline versions, CPU threading, pinned-memory/cache policy, kernel details, warm-up and repetition protocol, and random seeds. The stated code reference is also rendered only as a stray “a” with no usable link. Additionally, Appendix B.3 says max pooling of similarity triggers more corrections under the rule C_i < τ; mathematically, max pooling should trigger no more corrections than mean pooling, so the method description or reported interpretation is inconsistent.

strengths: Addresses an important systems problem: reducing the memory-transfer and selection costs of retrieval-based KV-cache compression.
The combination of one-step speculative retrieval, head-wise correction, hybrid CPU/GPU layouts, and double-buffered recall is coherent and practically motivated.
Accuracy experiments span multiple model families and long-input, long-generation, and reasoning benchmarks; at the tested budget, FreeKV is generally close to the full-cache model.
End-to-end A100 results show substantial speedups over several offloaded retrieval baselines, and the nested system ablation identifies hybrid layout as the dominant contributor.
The presentation is generally clear, with useful diagrams and supplementary analyses of query similarity, correction thresholds, and correction rates.
weaknesses: The central efficiency claim is not evaluated on the hardest reasoning workloads. At the chosen threshold, reported correction rates reach 0.35-0.52 on AIME24 and GPQA; because corrections put recall back on the critical path, latency measurements on these tasks are essential.

The core assumption is insufficiently validated: high cosine similarity between adjacent queries does not necessarily imply overlap of top-ranked KV pages. The paper omits selected-set overlap, retained attention mass, attention-output error, and correction-detector precision/recall analyses.

System evaluation is narrow: one A100/PCIe platform, only 7B-8B models, no serving workload, throughput or tail-latency results, variance across runs, peak-memory measurements, or profiling evidence for the claimed full latency hiding.

Baseline coverage and fairness are questionable. Quest is omitted even for configurations where it may fit; a feasible dense full-KV baseline is absent; ShadowKV is modified to rerun SVD periodically; and baseline implementation, tuning, and software-stack details are inadequate.

The claimed O(B) GPU-memory complexity is inaccurate because page summaries are retained on GPU and scale as O(L/p). No empirical memory-capacity study is provided despite memory scalability being a central motivation.

Accuracy differences are often small relative to likely sampling noise, yet no confidence intervals or significance tests are reported. Reasoning experiments use only 50 MATH500 and GPQA questions and 24 AIME questions, while LongBench inputs are truncated to 64K and LongGenBench relies on an unvalidated model judge.

Only one retrieval budget is studied, and task-specific correction thresholds appear selected using the reported benchmarks. Consequently, the claimed accuracy-efficiency Pareto frontier and robustness to unseen workloads are not established.

Most measured acceleration comes from the relatively standard hybrid-layout optimization, while speculative retrieval adds roughly 1.3-1.9x in the nested ablation. Novelty and attribution would be stronger with an optimized non-speculative baseline using the same layout and buffering.

Reproducibility is weak: the displayed code reference is broken ('Code is available a'), and important details about kernels, cache management, synchronization, baseline commits, and measurement methodology are missing.

strengths: The paper addresses an important deployment problem with a coherent co-design combining speculative KV retrieval, fine-grained correction, hybrid CPU/GPU layouts, and double-buffered recall.

The accuracy evaluation is unusually broad: it covers long-input, long-generation, and reasoning tasks; six main model variants; several strong dropping and retrieval baselines; and generally stays close to full-cache accuracy.

The reported systems gains are substantial—up to 13.7× over ArkVale—and experiments vary batch size, input length, and output length. Separate accuracy and efficiency ablations help identify the contribution of individual components.

The presentation is clear, the appendix provides useful query-similarity and correction-rate analyses, and no significant ethical concern is apparent. weaknesses: The headline speedup is not cleanly attributable to the proposed retrieval algorithm. Hybrid layout alone supplies up to 10.5×, whereas speculative retrieval adds at most 1.9× in the reported ablation. Baselines are not evaluated with the same layout and streaming optimizations, and several are materially modified; a common optimized backend is needed for a convincing comparison.

Accuracy and speed are not demonstrated at the same long-input configuration: LongBench accuracy uses S=W=128, while latency uses S=W=512, changing how many dynamically selected pages must be transferred. Moreover, only B=2048 and page size 32 are studied, and task-specific thresholds appear selected using the evaluation benchmarks. The claimed quality-efficiency frontier therefore lacks budget, page-size, and held-out threshold sweeps.

The O(B) GPU-memory claim is technically inaccurate. FreeKV retains min-max summaries for every page on GPU, requiring O(L/p) storage, so the total is at least O(B+L/p). Neither GPU nor CPU memory consumption is measured empirically.

The efficiency study is limited to one A100/PCIe host and batches of at most four. It omits full-cache latency and feasible Quest regimes, as well as decoding throughput/TPOT, continuous batching, run-to-run variation, and hardware/interconnect sensitivity.

No reasoning-task latency is reported even though correction rates reach 0.43–0.52 and correction recall lies on the critical path. Thus, the claim of fully hidden latency is not supported for precisely the difficult workloads used to motivate correction.

The stochastic accuracy results lack confidence intervals. MATH500 and GPQA are reduced to 50 examples without a reported sampling seed, and the LLM-judge protocol is under-specified; many claimed improvements are small enough to plausibly be noise.

The correction rule is insufficiently validated: high query cosine does not itself establish selected-page overlap, and no overlap or false-negative analysis is given. There is also an internal inconsistency: with correction triggered by C<τ, max-pooling cosine similarities cannot trigger more corrections than mean pooling as the appendix claims.

Reproducibility is incomplete: the abstract's code reference is malformed or missing, and software versions, implementation details, and baseline-performance validation are insufficient. These concerns slightly outweigh the otherwise strong empirical contribution.
